nuggets.text: The Leathernecks are the only college team whose official nickname comes from a branch of the U.S. military.
The Leathernecks got their name in 1927, when coach Ray Hanson, a Marine officer, asked the U.S. Navy for permission to use it.
The Leathernecks have two bulldog mascots: Colonel Rock, a live bulldog, and Rocky, a costumed one.
Hanson Field, home of the Leathernecks, is ringed by a hillside that seats thousands of extra fans.
A statue of two-time Olympic gold medalist Lee Calhoun, a former WIU track coach, stands outside the Leathernecks' Hanson Field.
Leathernecks coach Joe Davis was an Adrian College quarterback who later played pro football in Austria and in arena leagues.
Leathernecks QB Kennedy McGill arrived from Central Washington as the reigning Lone Star Conference Offensive Player of the Year.
Kennedy McGill ran for three touchdowns and threw two more as the Leathernecks opened 2026 with a 65-14 win over Northwestern College.
Leathernecks WR Christian Anaya has a catch of more than 45 yards in each of the team's first two games this season.
Leathernecks DB Jake Kruger picked off two passes in the season-opening win over Northwestern College.
